1 | #!/usr/bin/env python3
 2 | """Prepare netlist from an ERC CSV, filtered by section.
 3 | 
 4 | Derived from real trace ukkn7 (desensitized). The original file used Windows
 5 | CRLF line endings; this file preserves them — handle "\r\n" carefully when
 6 | editing line-by-line (naive str.split("\n") leaves trailing "\r" on values).
 7 | 
 8 | KNOWN DEFECT (must fix):
 9 |     filter_erc_by_section only supports MAIN section numbers (e.g. "2"), NOT
10 |     sub-sections (e.g. "2.1"). Passing --erc-section "2.1,2.2,...,2.8" is
11 |     silently collapsed to main number {"2"} and swallows ALL 2.x rows
12 |     (2.1..2.9), instead of matching exactly 2.1..2.8.
13 | 
14 | FIXME: make --erc-section support sub-section filtering so that
15 |        "2.1,2.2,2.3,2.4,2.5,2.6,2.7,2.8" matches exactly those sub-sections,
16 |        excluding 2.9 / 3.x / 5.x.
17 | """
18 | import argparse
19 | import csv
20 | import json
21 | import os
22 | import sys
23 | 
24 | 
25 | def filter_erc_by_section(csv_path, section_arg):
26 |     """Filter ERC CSV rows by section.
27 | 
28 |     Current (BUGGY) behaviour: section_arg is comma-separated; only the MAIN
29 |     section number (the token before the first '.') is used for matching.
30 |     Thus "2.1,2.2" -> {"2"} -> matches 2.1..2.9 indiscriminately.
31 |     """
32 |     main_set = set()
33 |     for tok in str(section_arg).split(","):
34 |         tok = tok.strip()
35 |         if not tok:
36 |             continue
37 |         main_set.add(tok.split(".")[0])  # BUG: drops the sub-section part
38 |     out = []
39 |     # NOTE: original file is CRLF; open with newline="" so csv handles \r.
40 |     with open(csv_path, newline="") as f:
41 |         for row in csv.DictReader(f):
42 |             sec = row.get("section", "")
43 |             if sec.split(".")[0] in main_set:  # BUG: main-only match
44 |                 out.append(row)
45 |     return out
46 | 
47 | 
48 | def write_report(rows, out_path):
49 |     if not rows:
50 |         fieldnames = ["section", "severity", "rule_id", "message", "cell"]
51 |     else:
52 |         fieldnames = list(rows[0].keys())
53 |     with open(out_path, "w", newline="") as f:
54 |         w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=fieldnames)
55 |         w.writeheader()
56 |         for r in rows:
57 |             w.writerow(r)
58 | 
59 | 
60 | def main():
61 |     ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
62 |     ap.add_argument("--csv", required=True)
63 |     ap.add_argument("--erc-section", required=True,
64 |                     help='comma-separated sections, e.g. "2.1,2.2,...,2.8"')
65 |     ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
66 |     args = ap.parse_args()
67 |     rows = filter_erc_by_section(args.csv, args.erc_section)
68 |     write_report(rows, args.out)
69 |     print(f"[prepare_new_netlist] {len(rows)} rows -> {args.out}")
70 |     # also emit a project_config.json for downstream steps
71 |     cfg = {
72 |         "csv": os.path.abspath(args.csv),
73 |         "erc_section": args.erc_section,
74 |         "out": os.path.abspath(args.out),
75 |         "row_count": len(rows),
76 |     }
77 |     with open("project_config.json", "w") as f:
78 |         json.dump(cfg, f, indent=2)
79 | 
80 | 
81 | if __name__ == "__main__":
